source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"An intermediate-acting insulin suspension that is normally cloudy after gentle resuspension","B":"A clear insulin solution that should be warmed before injection whenever cloudiness develops","C":"A contaminated insulin product that should always be discarded whenever it looks uniformly white","D":"A long-acting insulin solution that should remain completely clear and never require mixing"}}
source_row.rationale: NPH insulin is a suspension (intermediate-acting) and is normally cloudy/uniformly white after gentle mixing, unlike clear rapid- or long-acting insulins. It should be gently rolled between the hands or inverted (not shaken vigorously, which can cause bubbling and inaccurate dosing) to evenly resuspend the particles before drawing up the dose.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed HUMULIN N instructions: white/cloudy suspension; gently roll and invert to resuspend; accessed 2026-08-14.
